title.en: Explain the ABO and Rh grouping
Outline the clotting cascade and the nature of lymph

say.en: Before any transfusion the hospital cross-matches the donor and the patient. A wrong match can make the blood clump. Why? In this lesson: Explain the ABO and Rh grouping.
Identify universal donors and recipients.
Outline the clotting cascade and the nature of lymph.

body.en: ABO grouping depends on two surface antigens on RBCs, A and B, and natural antibodies in plasma. Group A has antigen A and anti-B; group B has antigen B and anti-A; group AB has both antigens and no antibodies; group O has neither antigen but both antibodies. So O is the universal donor and AB the universal recipient. The Rh antigen is present on the RBCs of nearly 80 per cent of humans (Rh+). An Rh− mother carrying an Rh+ foetus can be sensitised during her first delivery; in later pregnancies her anti-Rh antibodies can destroy foetal RBCs — erythroblastosis foetalis. Giving the mother anti-Rh antibodies immediately after the first delivery prevents it.
body.kn: ಎಬಿಒ ಗುಂಪು ಕೆಂಪು ರಕ್ತಕಣಗಳ ಮೇಲಿನ A ಮತ್ತು B ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕಗಳನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ. O ಗುಂಪು ಸಾರ್ವತ್ರಿಕ ದಾನಿ, AB ಗುಂಪು ಸಾರ್ವತ್ರಿಕ ಸ್ವೀಕರ್ತ. ಸುಮಾರು 80% ಜನರು Rh ಧನಾತ್ಮಕ. Rh ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕ ತಾಯಿ ಮತ್ತು Rh ಧನಾತ್ಮಕ ಭ್ರೂಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಿಥ್ರೋಬ್ಲಾಸ್ಟೋಸಿಸ್ ಫೀಟಾಲಿಸ್ ಬರಬಹುದು.

points.en: AB: both antigens, no antibodies — universal recipient
O: no antigens, both antibodies — universal donor

say.en: The ABO group depends on antigens A and B on red cells and the natural antibodies in plasma.
So group O can give to everyone, and group AB can receive from everyone.
Rh incompatibility: an Rh-negative mother with an Rh-positive baby gets sensitised at the first delivery. A later Rh-positive baby is at risk.
Clotting is a cascade. Platelet factors lead to thrombokinase, which turns prothrombin into thrombin; thrombin turns fibrinogen into fibrin threads.
Fluid that leaks from capillaries becomes tissue fluid; lymph vessels collect it and return it to the major veins.
The teacher tabulates the ABO groups, draws the Rh and clotting flowcharts, and shows how tissue fluid becomes lymph.

caption.en: A donor's red cells are safe only if the recipient's plasma has no antibody against their antigens. If it does, the red cells clump (agglutinate). Group O cells carry no A or B antigen; group AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibody.
caption.kn: ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸುವವರ ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾದಲ್ಲಿ ದಾನಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕಗಳ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ. ಇಲ್ಲವಾದರೆ ಕೆಂಪು ಕೋಶಗಳು ಗುಂಪುಗೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. O ಗುಂಪಿನ ಕೋಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ A ಅಥವಾ B ಪ್ರತಿಜನಕ ಇಲ್ಲ; AB ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯ ಇಲ್ಲ.

body.en: At an injury, platelets release certain factors that start the clotting mechanism. A cascade of reactions involving several plasma factors produces an enzyme complex, thrombokinase, which converts inactive prothrombin into thrombin. Thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads, which form a mesh trapping dead and damaged formed elements — the clot or coagulum. Calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.
body.kn: ಗಾಯವಾದಾಗ ಕಿರುತಟ್ಟೆಗಳು ಕೆಲವು ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಥ್ರಾಂಬೋಕೈನೇಸ್ ಪ್ರೋಥ್ರಾಂಬಿನ್ ಅನ್ನು ಥ್ರಾಂಬಿನ್ ಆಗಿ, ಥ್ರಾಂಬಿನ್ ಫೈಬ್ರಿನೋಜೆನ್ ಅನ್ನು ಫೈಬ್ರಿನ್ ಆಗಿ ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಕ್ಯಾಲ್ಸಿಯಂ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಮುಖ್ಯ.

body.en: As blood passes through capillaries, some water and small water-soluble substances move out into the spaces between cells, leaving the larger proteins and most formed elements behind. This fluid is *tissue fluid* or interstitial fluid. It has the same mineral distribution as plasma. A system of lymphatic vessels collects it and drains it back into the major veins; the fluid in this system is called lymph. Lymph is colourless, contains specialised lymphocytes for immunity, and carries absorbed fats from the intestinal villi through lacteals.
body.kn: ಲೋಮನಾಳಗಳಿಂದ ನೀರು ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ ವಸ್ತುಗಳು ಜೀವಕೋಶಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ಜಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸೋರಿ ಅಂಗಾಂಶ ದ್ರವವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ದುಗ್ಧನಾಳಗಳು ಇದನ್ನು ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ ಸಿರೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಹಿಂದಿರುಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ದುಗ್ಧರಸ ಬಣ್ಣರಹಿತ, ಲಿಂಫೋಸೈಟ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕೊಬ್ಬನ್ನು ಸಾಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

heading.en: Blood, Blood Groups, Coagulation and Lymph

tagline.en: Plasma and its proteins, RBCs, WBCs and platelets with their numbers and roles, ABO and Rh grouping, erythroblastosis foetalis, how blood clots, and tissue fluid and lymph.

myth.en: Erythroblastosis foetalis occurs in an Rh+ve mother carrying an Rh−ve baby, and the first baby is always affected.

truth.en: It occurs when the mother is Rh−ve and the foetus is Rh+ve. The first baby is usually safe; danger comes in later Rh+ve pregnancies. The mother's body makes anti-Rh antibodies only after it meets Rh+ve foetal cells, which mostly happens at the first delivery. Those antibodies then attack the next Rh+ve foetus.

say.en: Plasma 55% (fibrinogen, globulins, albumins); serum = plasma minus clotting factors.
RBC 5–5.5 million/mm³, life 120 days; WBC 6000–8000/mm³; platelets 1.5–3.5 lakh/mm³.
Neutrophils most and basophils fewest WBCs; neutrophils and monocytes are phagocytic.
O is universal donor, AB universal recipient; Rh−ve mother + Rh+ve foetus can cause erythroblastosis foetalis.
Clotting: thrombokinase → prothrombin to thrombin → fibrinogen to fibrin, with Ca²⁺. Lymph drains tissue fluid back to veins.

Actually: It occurs when the mother is Rh−ve and the foetus is Rh+ve. The first baby is usually safe; danger comes in later Rh+ve pregnancies. problem.en: Blood samples are tested with anti-A and anti-B sera. Sample P clumps with anti-A only; sample Q clumps with both; sample R clumps with neither. Find each blood group and say which sample can be given to all three people in an emergency.

steps.en: Clumping with anti-A means antigen A is present. P has only antigen A → group A.
Q has both antigens A and B → group AB.
R has neither antigen → group O.
Group O RBCs carry no A or B antigen, so R is the universal donor.

answer.en: P = A, Q = AB, R = O; sample R (group O) can be given to all three

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Blood samples are tested with anti-A and anti-B sera. Sample P clumps with anti-A only; sample Q clumps with both; sample R clumps with neither. Find each blood group and say which sample can be given to all three people in an emergency.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Blood samples are tested with anti-A and anti-B sera. Sample P clumps with anti-A only; sample Q clumps with both; sample R clumps with neither. Find each blood group and say which sample can be given to all three people in an emergency.
Clumping with anti-A means antigen A is present. P has only antigen A gives group A.
Q has both antigens A and B gives group AB.
R has neither antigen gives group O.
Group O RBCs carry no A or B antigen, so R is the universal donor.
So the answer is P equals A, Q equals AB, R equals O; sample R group O can be given to all three.
